ojluni-time.why: TestNG reads a data provider's generic return type, Iterator<Object[]>, and casts its type argument to Class. AOSP's libcore.reflect.GenericSignatureParser makes a GenericArrayTypeImpl for every array type argument and nothing resolves it to a Class, so the Wasm tier, which runs that bytecode, skips these tests (ClassCastException). The JS tier's reflection spec answers Object[].class.
ojluni-time.because: GenericArrayTypeImpl cannot be cast to java.lang.Class

ojluni-time.why: These compare System.currentTimeMillis with Clock.systemUTC() readings taken moments apart; on a loaded host either tier fails them in some runs.

guava.why: The JS tier's toArray(T[]) does not throw ArrayStoreException for an array whose element type the elements do not extend (JUnit: 'toArray(notAssignableTo[]) should throw'); the Wasm tier runs the AOSP bytecode, which does.

The JS tier throws UnsupportedOperationException from replaceAll on a ConcurrentSkipListMap submap (the Map default reaching an immutable entry's setValue, apparently, where ConcurrentMap's default is the more specific one); the Wasm tier runs the AOSP bytecode and passes.

jsr166.why: On the JS tier an asynchronous CompletableFuture stage fails with NoSuchMethodError: unsafe-fallthrough java/lang/Thread.nextThreadNum()I (the common pool names its threads through a private static member of Thread that the JS tier's Thread spec lacks); on strands the Wasm tier runs Thread's own bytecode.

The JS tier's toArray(T[]) does not throw ArrayStoreException for an array whose element type the elements do not extend (JUnit: 'toArray(notAssignableTo[]) should throw'); the Wasm tier runs the AOSP bytecode, which does.

luni-util.why: The JS tier models Integer, Long and String as JS numbers and strings: comparing an Integer with a String does not throw the ClassCastException the test expects (JUnit: 'ClassCastException expected'); on the Wasm tier they are Java objects.

On the JS tier Class.getMethod("values") on an enum throws NoSuchMethodException (JUnit: RuntimeException: java.lang.NoSuchMethodException: values); on the Wasm tier the enum's own values() is a method of the class.

The JS tier's Strings are JS strings, so new String(s) is the same reference as s (JUnit: 'failure of non-equality of IdentityHashMaps one and two', 'Returned true for copy of valid key', 'expected not same'); on the Wasm tier a String is an object with an identity of its own.
A Throwable deserializes on the JS tier with its message or cause lost (JUnit: expected:<for serialization test> but was:<null>).
The JS tier's Thread accepts a null name, so new Timer(null, true) does not throw the NullPointerException the test expects (JUnit: fail()).

luni-io.why: The class declares a private static suite(). The JS tier's Class.getMethod("suite") returns that private method, so JUnit runs the suite; AOSP and the JDK do not find it, JUnit reports 'No runnable methods', and the Wasm tier runs AOSP's Class.getMethod.
The JS tier cannot deserialize a proxy class that was an interface (JUnit: InvalidClassException: java.lang.reflect.$Proxy1; no valid constructor).
A Throwable deserializes on the JS tier with its message or cause lost (JUnit: expected:<java.lang.Throwable: java.io.IOError> but was:<null>; expected:<serialization test> but was:<null>).

The default serialVersionUID, a hash over the class's methods, differs on the JS tier (JUnit: expected:<-4558121473827608582> but was:<-2829093031046158691>): its reflection lists the class's methods differently.

writeUnshared must write an object again each time, and on the JS tier it does not for the Strings the test makes with new String (JUnit: 'oa[0] != oa[1] expected not same'): their identity is that of their value there.
The JS tier's compiled code for the test fails with a NullPointerException of its own (null is not an object (evaluating 'F.v[K[0]][K[1]]')).

luni-nio-file.why: The JS tier's serialized form of a Throwable differs from the golden stream the test compares it with (JUnit: ComparisonFailure on the hex dump); the Wasm tier serializes AOSP's own fields.

luni-net.why: The JS tier's serialized Inet6Address differs from what the test expects (JUnit fails it); the Wasm tier serializes AOSP's own fields.
